question: For the matrices $$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\0&1\end{bmatrix},\quad B=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\3&1\end{bmatrix},\quad C=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\2&3\end{bmatrix},$$ calculate $(AB)C$ and $A(BC)$ through direct multiplication and establish that matrix multiplication is associative for these matrices.
explanation:
Evaluation of $(AB)C$

First calculate $AB$: $$AB=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\0&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\3&1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1(2)+2(3)&1(-1)+2(1)\\0(2)+1(3)&0(-1)+1(1)\end{bmatrix}$$ $$=\begin{bmatrix}8&1\\3&1\end{bmatrix}$$ Therefore, $$(AB)C=\begin{bmatrix}8&1\\3&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\2&3\end{bmatrix}$$ $$=\begin{bmatrix}8(1)+1(2)&8(0)+1(3)\\3(1)+1(2)&3(0)+1(3)\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}10&3\\5&3\end{bmatrix}$$

Evaluation of $A(BC)$

Now, $$BC=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\3&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\2&3\end{bmatrix}$$ $$=\begin{bmatrix}2(1)+(-1)(2)&2(0)+(-1)(3)\\3(1)+1(2)&3(0)+1(3)\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0&-3\\5&3\end{bmatrix}$$ Hence, $$A(BC)=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\0&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}0&-3\\5&3\end{bmatrix}$$ $$=\begin{bmatrix}1(0)+2(5)&1(-3)+2(3)\\0(0)+1(5)&0(-3)+1(3)\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}10&3\\5&3\end{bmatrix}$$ Since both products are equal, $$(AB)C=A(BC)$$ Thus, matrix multiplication is associative for the given matrices.
